A_target.statement:
Let $\mathbf A$ be a real $m \times n$ matrix with [[Definition:Linearly Independent Set|linearly independent]] columns.
Then $\mathbf A = \mathbf Q \mathbf R$, with $\mathbf Q$ having [[Definition:Orthonormal Subset|orthonormal]] columns and $\mathbf R$ [[Definition:Upper Triangular Matrix|upper triangular]] with positive diagonal.

B_source.statement:
Let $\mathbf a_1, \ldots, \mathbf a_n$ be linearly independent in an inner product space.
Then [[Gram-Schmidt Orthogonalization]] produces orthonormal $\mathbf q_1, \ldots, \mathbf q_n$ with $\map {\operatorname {span} } {\mathbf q_1, \ldots, \mathbf q_k} = \map {\operatorname {span} } {\mathbf a_1, \ldots, \mathbf a_k}$ for each $k$.

object_map.reformulation: Rewrite the Gram-Schmidt recursion in matrix form: each column is a combination of the first k orthonormal vectors.

validity_conditions: Linear independence ensures that no residual vanishes, so the diagonal of R is positive.
Numerically, Householder reflections compute the same factorization more stably.
proof_plan: Apply the source result to the columns $\mathbf a_1, \ldots, \mathbf a_n$ of $\mathbf A$.

As $\mathbf a_k \in \map {\operatorname {span} } {\mathbf q_1, \ldots, \mathbf q_k}$:
:$\displaystyle \mathbf a_k = \sum_{j \mathop \le k} r_{j k} \mathbf q_j, \quad r_{j k} = \innerprod {\mathbf a_k} {\mathbf q_j}$
$r_{k k}$ is the length of the residual of $\mathbf a_k$ after projecting onto the earlier span, which is positive by linear independence.
